backend.measure: sum of the image's unpacked layer sizes (docker history), in MB (10^6 bytes)
backend.justification: Re-measured in P10 when boto3 joined the runtime dependencies (ADR 019): about 277 MB unpacked, about 92 MB compressed (docker save | gzip). Roughly 148 MB is the Debian and Python base image and about 128 MB the locked production virtual environment. Of that, the AWS SDK is about 26 MB (botocore 22 MB of service descriptions, boto3, s3transfer, jmespath, dateutil), SQLAlchemy 23 MB, cryptography 16 MB, asyncpg 11 MB, pypdfium2 (P9) about 6 MB with its PDFium library, plus precompiled bytecode because the runtime filesystem is read-only. The first baseline (2026-09-21, 229 MB) predates pypdfium2 and boto3. The application code, migrations and alembic.ini are under 1 MB. The ceiling is the baseline plus about 20%: enough for ordinary dependency patch updates, tight enough to catch accidental bloat such as a forgotten cache, a dev dependency or a copied directory. Deliberately not optimised further. LangGraph (P12) will grow the image again: raise the ceiling in the same change, re-measure, and rewrite this justification (the test refuses a ceiling more than 25% above the recorded baseline).

frontend.measure: sum of the image's unpacked layer sizes (docker history), in MB (10^6 bytes)
frontend.justification: First clean build of frontend/Dockerfile on nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.31.6-alpine3.24: about 59.7 MB unpacked, about 23 MB compressed (docker save | gzip). Almost all of it is the base image: roughly 9 MB Alpine, 6 MB nginx and 44 MB of nginx's own packages and modules. The site itself (the Next.js static export, 0.76 MB) and nginx.conf are under 1 MB, and there is no Node, npm or node_modules in the runtime stage. The ceiling is the baseline plus 20%: enough to absorb a base image patch update, tight enough to catch a leaked build stage (a Node runtime alone would add well over 100 MB) or a copied directory. Deliberately not optimised further. The test refuses a ceiling more than 25% above the recorded baseline.
